gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sc: Lowercase letters with the stature of cast iron capitals define Edo SZ, each stroke glowing like neon glass tubing. And Noto Sans SC, with chalky curves that stop short of closing, wants a slightly larger size.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height and curves with wide, unclosed mouths. Noto Sans Soyombo can stay modest in size beneath Edo SZ, whose unmodulated line runs across every glyph.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar reads clean and approachable, its curves leaving daylight like a rope's open bight, with short ascender stems. Edo SZ, cut at one depth like an engraver's line, anchors the top.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Clean in spirit, Noto Sans Syloti Nagri has short ascenders and an a whose lower bowl opens to breathe. Edo SZ is a thread of ink; the body's paragraphs flow without snagging.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Bent paperclip meets blown glass: Edo SZ keeps its line uniform, while Noto Sans Syriac fills its lowercase bowls like bulbs. Its s shapes take wide, easy turns, so paragraphs glide.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Sturdy, uniform strokes: Edo SZ matches horizontals to verticals, while Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps its curve endings well apart. One shouts in iron, the other speaks lightly beside it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Noto Sans Syriac Western reads crisp, its terminals held far from the stroke. Beneath Edo SZ, whose outline is thick throughout, those small letters packed with height like bundled cable hold the layout steady.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Edo SZ writes with constant pen pressure, its lowercase standing like cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa supplies open curves with clear gaps, its lowercase filling most of the height.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Approachable at heart, Noto Sans Tai Viet has short ascenders, a large x-height, and terminals pulled back from where curves close. Edo SZ weights diagonals like uprights, so the body can stay small.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri leaves a generously open curve on every small round letter, with a high-waisted lowercase. Edo SZ, its joins slim as a pipe cleaner, leads the way.
